correctness.rationale: For m>=2 the ambient metric of K_{1,m} forces a >=3-point selected subset containing the center to fix it, while leaf-only partial maps are arbitrary partial permutations; center-moving maps are exactly 2m singletons and m² exchanged-role center/leaf arrows. Center-fixed maps are non-nilpotent, and among two-arrow center-moving maps precisely m(m-1) chains a->0->b with a!=b are nilpotent. Nilpotent leaf maps decompose uniquely into directed paths; labeled path species yields H_{m,L}(u)=m![z^m]exp(sum_{j<=L}u^(j-1)z^j). Differences of H give joint rank/index counts plus two exceptional corrections. Summing gives all-rank counts, total nilpotents m![z^m]exp(z/(1-z))+m(m+1), and order 2m![z^m]exp(z/(1-z))/(1-z)+m²+2m. For length extremes, independent Poisson path-component counts Z_j~Pois(rho^j) conditioned on sum j Z_j=m use rho/(1-rho)^2=m; local CLT at scale m^(3/4) makes conditioning negligible for absence of paths longer than .5 sqrt(m) log m+x sqrt(m), whose Poisson mean tends to exp(-x), giving Gumbel. Coefficient ratio via added geometric component gives nilpotent density ~1/(2sqrt(m)). Direct independent complete star-metric partial map enumeration gives (monoid order,nil count)=(22,9),(83,25),(442,93) for m=2,3,4 and agrees with every rank/index profile.
